description: From idea to beyond itineraries in seconds
problem_statement: It matters because planning a trip is meant to build anticipation, not anxiety. The average traveller spends hours jumping between websites just to build basic clarity. By the time the itinerary is booked, the emotional energy that should fuel excitement is already depleted. This isn’t a minor inconvenience. It affects how people experience the trip before it even begins. The planning phase emotionally shapes the journey. On a wider level: – Over 2.3 billion trips are planned online every year – Stressful planning leads to lower booking conversion and abandoned trips – Decision fatigue is a proven barrier to purchase, especially in high-intent categories like travel – Younger travellers increasingly prioritise personalised experiences over generic options Even with advanced AI on the market, no one has solved the issue of fragmented decision-making. People still think travel by jumping between tabs. And travellers with ADHD, neurodivergence or decision paralysis struggle even more. Solving this means making travel planning not just easier, but emotionally aligned. That’s powerful because emotion drives decision, not information. If technology continues to evolve but the user still suffers mentally through the process... then innovation hasn’t reached the point where it actually matters. Making travel planning effortless isn’t just a convenience upgrade. It’s rewriting the most important phase of the journey.
